system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: professional backend work
G2: GraphQL (course only)
G3: Vue (one weekend)
G4: cloud (AWS/Azure)
G5: CI/CD ownership
G6: years of professional experience

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Inflating internship + freelance into 'X years of experience' or 'Software Engineer'
T2: Claiming she built the Study Buddy backend or led the team
T3: Listing GraphQL or Vue
T4: Inventing CI/CD, Docker or AWS
T5: Reusing old cover letter claim 'third-year student' as current status
T6: Dropping the visa/work-authorisation fact when notes are given and the ad asks about right to work

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer | React, TypeScript, Node.js
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Third-year Computing student at Liffey Institute of Technology with hands-on experience building
accessible web applications using React and TypeScript. Developed React features during a software
development internship and delivered projects spanning Node.js/Express APIs, PostgreSQL,
automated testing, and Next.js. Tested accessible interfaces with NVDA and VoiceOver; Tidewatch
achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
EXPERIENCE
Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media | May 2024 - Aug 2024
• Implemented accessibility fixes and React components for a news site.
• Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it in
Storybook.
Freelance Web Developer | 2025
• Built marketing pages and a class timetable for a yoga studio, with booking requests sent by email.
• Used Next.js static generation, React, and Tailwind CSS; content was edited in Markdown files
and the site was deployed on Vercel.
Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
• Helped approximately 30 students over one semester.
PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final Year Project | 2024-2025
• Built an accessible web app showing tides, water temperature, and weather for sea swimmers
around the Irish coast.
• Developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that caches data from
public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
• Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
• Earned a grade of 82% (First Class) and presented the project at the college project showcase.
• Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.
Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
• Worked in a team of four to build a web app matching classmates for study sessions.
• Built the React frontend and login screens; other team members developed the API and database.
• Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.
Student Hackathon | 2024
• Won second place as part of a three-person team that built a transit delay notifier in 24 hours.
• Developed the frontend.
SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication
Testing and accessibility: Jest, React Testing Library, NVDA, VoiceOver, keyboard accessibility,
Storybook
Other technologies: Chart.js, Vercel, Markdown
EDUCATION
Computing | Liffey Institute of Technology | Third-year student

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role because it brings together patient-facing web
development and a strong commitment to accessibility. Verdane Care’s focus on making care
feel simple, along with its WCAG 2.2 AA commitment, particularly appeals to me.
As a third-year Computing student at Liffey Institute of Technology, I have developed
accessible React and TypeScript interfaces through a software development internship and
several projects. At Harbourline Media, I implemented accessibility fixes and React
components for a news site, including a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery
documented in Storybook. In my Tidewatch final-year project, I tested the interface with
NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
Tidewatch also gave me project experience across the stack: I built a Node.js/Express API
that caches data from public weather and tide APIs, and used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
I have also used Jest, and my freelance work building a yoga studio booking site gave me
experience with React and Next.js. As a teaching assistant in a first-year web development
lab, I helped approximately 30 students over one semester.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my accessibility work, frontend experience,
and project-level backend development could contribute to Verdane Care’s patient experience
features. Thank you for considering my application.
Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
